topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the core learning objectives concerning cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the mechanisms, clinical efficacy, and systemic limitations of traditional surgical, radiation, and cytotoxic approaches to cancer management.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent cancer-specific defects in growth signalling, cell cycle checkpoints, and DNA damage repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors, Oncogene Addiction, and Drug Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting driver oncogenes and describe the molecular mechanisms through which tumor cells develop resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered antibodies are utilized to selectively recognize tumor surface antigens to inhibit oncogenic signaling and deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell-Directed Approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the immunological basis of anti-tumor immunity and detail cellular and molecular strategies to reactivate or engineer T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Current Challenges, Treatment Evolution, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review persistent obstacles in cancer management, historical gains in patient survival, and emerging considerations for future therapeutic paradigms.
